annotations.title: Fill the tax declaration for the person to send

description:
Start the fill of one prepared tax declaration in the person's own Chrome, from their WhatsApp turn. Well opens the authority's site there, the person signs in themselves, Well types the boxes of the prepared declaration and stops before the send: the person checks the form and clicks Envoyer themselves. Use it only when the person's own message asks Well to fill or file the declaration, after the declaration was prepared.

Pass `declaration_type` and the `document_id` the prepare tool returned. Never pass an amount: Well reads the figures from the stored declaration and checks them again against the declaration's blocking checks, and the CA3 against the posted ledger too. Never say the declaration is filed or sent. On success, `outcome` `queued` means nothing runs yet: never say the fill started, and word the reply from `message`. `waits_for_extension: true` means the person's Chrome has no Well extension that takes the fill yet: the fill starts by itself once they install or update it, with no new ask, and `message` says what to tell them.

On `refusal`: `no_extension`, the PDF already sent is the path, the person files it themselves. `extension_outdated`, the PDF already sent is the path, and an update of the Well extension lets Well fill the next one. `return_changed` or `not_fileable`, prepare the declaration again and show the new figures. `prior_credit_unconfirmed`, line 22 waits for the person: ask once what « le crédit reporté de ta déclaration précédente » was, naming no line, prepare the declaration again with the `prior_credit_euros` they give, and show the new figures. `check_blocked`, the declaration fails a blocking check listed in `rule_ids`: say what to correct and fill nothing. `already_filed`, never fill again. `period_already_filed`, say plainly it is filed on the date in `filed_on` (day/month). `filing_live`, another fill runs: start nothing. `handed_over_pending`, the filled form waits in the person's Chrome: tell them to send it from that tab. `not_validated`, show the prepared figures and ask the person to confirm them in a new message. `confirmation_required`, ask the one numbered question the `error` text gives and end the turn. Follow the `error` text for any other refusal.

When the token authorizes one workspace, call this directly — no workspace call is needed first. When it authorizes several, this read will not guess which one you mean: pass `workspace_id` on the call.

conversation_id.description: The conversation id returned by the previous Well result, in its meta under well/conversation_id, in its structuredContent, or in its JSON text block. Pass it back on every call in the same conversation, including a call a card makes, so the chosen workspace and the earlier answers still apply. It decides the conversation on its own: nothing the host states about the session replaces it. Omit it only on the first call of a conversation.

declaration_type.description: The declaration to fill: `fr-vat-ca3` for the CA3 VAT return prepared by well_prepare_vat_return, `fr-micro-turnover` for the URSSAF micro-entrepreneur turnover declaration prepared by well_prepare_micro_declaration.

document_id.description: The `document_id` of the prepared declaration, as its prepare tool returned it in this conversation.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A retried write with the same key returns the original result instead of re-applying the operation.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace. Omit when the token authorizes one workspace. Required when it authorizes several — a write lands in exactly one workspace and this call would not say which.

workspace_scope.description: Restrict this call to the family: the token's primary workspace plus the company workspaces under it that you are a member of. Unrelated authorized workspaces drop out of the read; row reads merge across the family, while a per-workspace figure still reports exactly one workspace.

name: well_create_declaration_filing

conversation_id.description: The conversation this result belongs to. Pass it back as the conversation_id argument on every later Well call in the same conversation.

conversation_id_note.description: Present only when the server opened a fresh lane, stating that no choice recorded earlier was read.

conversation_id_source.description: Where the conversation id came from: the host's own request meta, the caller's argument, or a fresh lane the server opened.

newly_connected.description: Tools that connected to this workspace since the last result and that no session was told about yet, oldest first. Present only when at least one tool is new. The connected-line rule says when to tell an entry; when it does, one line per entry, in the person's language: "<name> is connected.". Never fold several entries into one sentence. Each entry comes back once, on one result only: never repeat its line later.

resolved_workspace.description: The workspace that answered, when the caller named none and the token authorizes several.
